title: Gandhiji on the salt tax (Source 3)
body:
Read the extract from Mahatma Gandhi's writing on the salt tax and answer the question that follows.

"The volume of information being gained daily shows how wickedly the salt tax has been designed. In order to prevent the use of salt that has not paid the tax which is at times even fourteen times its value, the Government destroys the salt it cannot sell profitably. Thus it taxes the nation's vital necessity; it prevents the public from manufacturing it and destroys what nature manufactures without effort ... The salt monopoly is thus a fourfold curse. It deprives the people of a valuable easy village industry, involves wanton destruction of property that nature produces in abundance, the destruction itself means more national expenditure, and fourthly, to crown this folly, an unheard-of tax of more than 1,000 per cent is exacted from a starving people."
(The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, Vol. 49, as quoted in the NCERT chapter)

title: The Home Department watches the Salt March (Source 8)
body:
Read the extracts from the confidential Fortnightly Reports of the Home Department for March 1930 and answer the question that follows.

Bengal: "The reports from the districts show that the meetings that have been held excite little or no interest and leave no profound impression on the general population. It is noticeable, however, that ladies are attending these meetings in increasing numbers."
Madras: "General opinion inclines to regard his march as theatrical and his programme as impracticable, but as he is held in such personal reverence by the Hindu public generally, the possibility of arrest which he seems deliberately to be courting and its effect on the political situation are viewed with considerable misgiving."
Central Provinces and Berar: "In Nagpur these meetings were well attended and most of the schools and colleges were deserted on the 12th March to mark the inauguration of Gandhi's march."
United Provinces: "Political activity has undoubtedly intensified during the last fortnight."
